newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen down 84-92 bcf in weekly AGA.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen down 84-92 bcf in weekly AGA.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to fall by 84-92 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said Wednesday.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for a drawdown ranged widely from 60 bcf to 125 bcf for the week ended Dec 6.
"I think we'll see another decent draw this week. The HDDs (heating degree days) were slightly above-normal last week," said one Texas-based trader.

Last week's draw of 104 bcf left stocks at 217 bcf, or eight percent, below year-ago and surprised most players who expected inventories to decline by 70-80 bcf. The four week average drawdown is 70 bcf.
But traders said the stock gap to last year should close significantly in coming weeks, as weekly declines fail to match last December's weekly average draw of 142 bcf.
In last report, eastern stocks fell by 62 bcf to 86 percent of capacity but were still slightly above year-ago. Producing and consuming region west stocks continued to significantly lag 1995 levels.

For the same week last year, total inventories fell by 75 bcf, meaning a draw today in the expected range would widen the gap to last year to about 230 bcf. In 1995, eastern storage fell by 50 bcf, while producing stocks dropped by 16 bcf and western stocks by nine bcf.
